python3 tools/mem.py log "Cut rules, written before the first cut (stage D4 section 2); they go into tree-D4.md before any branch. (R0) Minimum group size: the default, 5; prior.md sets none, and I keep it, since 720 level-3 keys are held by 5 to 19 rooms and a higher floor would drop most change keys before reading them. (R1) A branch is keyed on an element's change key (op add-step, add-condition, link, restrict or contradict), read in the all-kinds matrix (the kind of add-condition, add-step and restrict lines is not relied on), at the deepest ladder level where 5 or more rooms meet on it. Arrow keys cannot key a branch (stage_D4.py resolves a key's target against the elements) and are read as context. Instantiate and absent keys specify; they change nothing, so they define no branch. (R2) A key becomes a branch only if the members' lines, read through out/_analysis/d4_key_lines.py, state one shared change to the element (a step, a condition or a link the statement does not hold, or holds only in part); otherwise the group is set aside with its reason. (R3) A subform is a level-3 child key held by 5 or more of the branch's members whose lines state a narrower change than the parent's. (R4) Corrections that meet only at the dimension or the bare target (P05's shape read, R01's joining) are groupings, not branches. (R5) A room in two branches that do not nest is a cross-link, generated by script with both keys as its reason. (R6) Order: by element, from the largest change-key group at level 4 downward; a leg ends at a safe stop after a logged move. (R7) The ground is the keys unless a cut's tier_history line declares the members' material. The branch's kind field is the majority kind of its members' lines on the key, reported and not relied on." --kind note 2>&1 | tail -n 1 && python3 out/_analysis/d4_key_lines.py --key add-step:K01:T4-001 --level 4 --children --limit 0 2>&1 | head -n 3
